name: St Aldhelm's College
eyebrow: End of term at St Aldhelm's
blurbs: The end of term, a priceless manuscript and a fellow who will not be returning next year.
The bell has rung for dinner. One scholar is still among the books, and will be for ever.
Centuries of learning, a college at war with itself and one very final examination.
Quiet, please. Somebody in this college is about to get away with murder.
Exams are over, the punts are out, and one tutor has marked a last paper.
Somewhere in the college a rare first edition has vanished, and so has a fellow.
Candlelight at high table, gossip over port and a death that nobody can explain.
Every scholar here has a theory. Only one of them knows what really happened.
The Master is retiring, the fellows are plotting, and one vote has just been permanently cast.
Nothing ever happens in this college. That is precisely why nobody noticed for hours.
A rival scholar arrives to read a paper. By the end of the evening, there is an obituary to write.
Some books here are chained in place. Some secrets ought to have been.
motives: a thesis had been copied, word for word, thirty years ago
the college silver had been quietly sold to pay a debt
the election for the new master was closer than anyone admitted
a medieval manuscript in the archive was a very modern forgery
a bequest to the college came with a clause nobody had read
a footnote in an old journal proved the great discovery was stolen
the college's oldest benefactor had made a fortune nobody could mention
a research student's notebook had been published under another name
the new master had promised the same post to three people
a chained book had been sold and replaced with a clever copy
an exam paper had been leaked, and one career had been built on it
a long-closed inquiry into a student's death had just been reopened
the rival's paper was about to demolish a lifetime of work
a college ghost story had been covering for a very real crime
the treasurer's books balanced only if nobody read them

A college notices nothing before the porter's morning round. {murderer} and {victim} had the {area} until then: {motive}.
{victim} had come to the {area} to check a reference. {murderer} had checked it first: {motive}.
The evening bell covered the rest. {murderer} left the {area} in time for evensong, because {motive}.

{murderer} has marked many final papers, but only one in the {area}: {motive}.
